errors.current: المدرسة = the school
errors.problem: the unvocalised key also covers الْمُدَرِّسَة 'the (female) teacher'; a learner tapping الْمُدَرِّسَة is told 'the school'
errors.fix: the school (al-madrasa); the teacher (f) (al-mudarrisa)

errors.current: الرجل = the man
errors.problem: key also covers الرِّجْل 'the leg, the foot' (the course glosses رجلي = my leg, so the body-part sense is in use)
errors.fix: the man (ar-rajul); the leg, the foot (ar-rijl)

errors.current: رجل = man; رجلان = two legs
errors.problem: رجل covers رَجُل 'man' and رِجْل 'leg'; رجلان covers رَجُلَانِ 'two men' and رِجْلَانِ 'two legs' — each gloss gives only one of the two and the pair is inconsistent (singular glossed as 'man', dual as 'legs')
errors.fix: رجل = a man (rajul); a leg, a foot (rijl) · رجلان = two men (rajulān); two legs (rijlān)

errors.current: العام = the general
errors.problem: الْعَام 'the year' (هَذَا الْعَام 'this year') is far more common for a beginner than the adjective; the key covers both
errors.fix: the year (al-ʿām); the general, the public (adjective)

errors.current: العالم = the world
errors.problem: key also covers الْعَالِم 'the scholar, the scientist' (the plural العلماء is glossed 'the scholars' in this same list)
errors.fix: the world (al-ʿālam); the scholar, the scientist (al-ʿālim)

errors.current: الدين = al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
errors.problem: glossed only as a name element from one sentence; الدِّين is the ordinary word 'religion, faith' (and الدَّيْن 'debt')
errors.fix: the religion, the faith (ad-dīn; also the second part of names such as Salah al-Din); the debt (ad-dayn)

errors.current: حرب = Harb (part of a street name in Cairo)
errors.problem: glossed only as a street name; حَرْب is the basic word 'war' (الحرب = the war is in this list)
errors.fix: war (ḥarb); also a surname, as in Talaat Harb Street in Cairo

errors.current: جد = (he) worked hard, strove
errors.problem: the basic reading of جد is جَدّ 'grandfather' (الجد, جدك, جدتي are all in this list); the verb جَدَّ is a sentence-specific leak
errors.fix: grandfather (jadd); (he) worked hard, strove (jadda); seriousness (jidd, as in bi-jidd 'seriously')

errors.current: جمع = (he) gathered, collected
errors.problem: in a grammar course جَمْع 'plural; gathering' is the reading a learner will meet most (الجمع = the plural, بالجمع = in the plural are in this list); the key covers both
errors.fix: (he) gathered, collected (jamaʿa); plural, gathering (jamʿ)

errors.current: جملا = a camel
errors.problem: key covers جَمَلًا 'a camel' and جُمَلًا 'sentences' (plural of جملة); in a language course the second is at least as likely
errors.fix: a camel (jamalan); sentences (jumalan, plural of jumla)

errors.current: درسنا = our lesson
errors.problem: key also covers دَرَسْنَا 'we studied', a form a beginner meets constantly; gloss gives only the noun
errors.fix: our lesson (darsunā); we studied (darasnā)

errors.current: المهمة = the important (f)
errors.problem: key also covers الْمَهَمَّة 'the task, the mission', a common noun
errors.fix: the important (f) (al-muhimma); the task, the mission (al-mahamma)

errors.current: أقدم = the oldest (before a noun)
errors.problem: key also covers أُقَدِّم 'I present, I submit, I offer' (Form II), frequent in the course's presentation/application scenes; the elative-only gloss is wrong there
errors.fix: older, oldest (aqdam); I present, I offer, I submit (uqaddim)

errors.current: أحمل = I download; حملت = I downloaded
errors.problem: the basic readings أَحْمِل 'I carry' and حَمَلْتُ 'I carried' are missing; 'download' is only the Form II reading (أُحَمِّل / حَمَّلْتُ) of one sentence
errors.fix: أحمل = I carry (aḥmil); I download (uḥammil) · حملت = I carried (ḥamaltu); I downloaded (ḥammaltu); also you carried / she carried (-ta, -ti, -at)

errors.current: خالتك = your aunt (mother's sister) ('your cousin')
errors.problem: the quoted alternative 'your cousin' is wrong (خالة is never cousin) — an editorial or sentence-translation note leaked into the gloss and contradicts the correct part
errors.fix: your aunt (mother's sister)

errors.current: تأخذها = take it (f; to a man)
errors.problem: تَأْخُذُهَا is a present-tense form ('you take it' / 'she takes it'), not an imperative; the imperative would be خُذْهَا. A beginner learns the wrong form
errors.fix: you take it (f) (to a man); she takes it

errors.path: تخف; تنس; تنسي; تقلقي; تغضبي; تشتر; تعط; تعطها; تحاول; تركض; تسجل; تشتريا; تقرؤوا; تقولوا
errors.current: تخف = be afraid (to a man); تنس = forget (to a man); تنسي = forget (to a woman); تقلقي = worry (to a woman); تغضبي = get angry (to a woman); تشتر = buy (to a man); تعط = give (to a man); تعطها = give her (to a man); تحاول = try (to a man); تركض = run (to a man); تسجل = score (to a man); تشتريا = buy (to two people); تقرؤوا = read (you all); تقولوا = say, tell (to several people)
errors.problem: these تـ forms are jussive/subjunctive present forms, which in the course appear after لا (don't…) or أن/لن; glossed as bare positive imperatives they teach the opposite meaning (لا تَخَفْ = don't be afraid, لا تَنْسَ = don't forget, لا تَقْلَقِي = don't worry) and a wrong form (the real imperatives are خَفْ, انْسَ, اشْتَرِ, أَعْطِ, حَاوِلْ, اركُضْ, سَجِّلْ, اشْتَرِيَا, اقْرَؤُوا, قُولُوا). تنم is the one entry that does say 'after don't' and shows the right pattern
errors.fix: pattern as in تنم: e.g. تخف = you fear (to a man) — after lā: lā takhaf 'don't be afraid'; تنس = you forget (to a man) — lā tansa 'don't forget'; تنسي = you forget (to a woman) — lā tansī 'don't forget'; تقلقي = you worry (to a woman) — lā taqlaqī 'don't worry'; تغضبي = you get angry (to a woman) — lā taghḍabī 'don't get angry'; تشتر = you buy (to a man, after lā/lam); تعط = you give (to a man, after lā/lam); تعطها = you give her/it (to a man, after lā/lam); تحاول = you try (to a man); she tries; تركض = you run (to a man); she runs; تسجل = you score, you record (to a man); she scores; تشتريا = you two buy (after an/lā); تقرؤوا = you (all) read (after an/lā); تقولوا = you (all) say (after an/lā)

(to a man); أوقف = stop! (to a man); سجل = scored (lit. recorded); تدرب = (he) practised ('practised')
errors.problem: for Forms II, IV, VIII and X the unvocalised past (he …) and the imperative (…!) are spelt the same, so each gloss is wrong for half the occurrences: اتَّصِلْ بِي 'call me!' gets '(he) called', ابْتَسَمَ 'he smiled' gets 'smile!'. تدرب also covers تُدَرِّب/تَتَدَرَّب 'you train, you practise'; سجل also covers سَجِّلْ 'register!/record!'
errors.fix: ابتسم = (he) smiled; smile! (to a man) · اتصل = (he) called, phoned; call! (to a man) · اتفق = (he) agreed; agree! (to a man) · اجتمع = (he) met (with); meet! (to a man) · افتتح = (he) opened (officially); open! · استعمل = (he) used; use! (to a man) · انتبه = (he) paid attention; watch out!, pay attention! (to a man) · أوقف = (he) stopped (something); stop! (to a man) · سجل = (he) scored, recorded, registered; record!, register! (to a man) · تدرب = (he) practised, trained; you practise (to a man)

errors.path: أتعبت; اتفقت; أحضرت; أخبرتك; أخطأت; استأجرت; استمعت; اشتريت; اشتريتها; أكلته; أكلتها; انكسرت; تعلمته; توقعت; حجزت; حصلت; خفت; دفعت; رأيت; رأيته; رأيتها; راجعت; ركبت; سافرت; سبحت; سجلته; سمعت; سمعته; سمعتها
errors.current: أتعبت = you tired, you troubled (to a man); اتفقت = (she) agreed (-i links to the next word); أحضرت = I brought; أخبرتك = I told you (to a man); أخطأت = you made a mistake (to a man); استأجرت = I rented; استمعت = I listened; اشتريت = I bought; اشتريتها = I bought it (f); أكلته = I ate it; أكلتها = I ate it (f); انكسرت = (she) broke, got broken; تعلمته = I learned it; توقعت = I expected; حجزت = (she) booked; حصلت = you got (to a man); خفت = I was afraid, I worried; دفعت = I paid; رأيت = you saw (to a man); رأيته = you saw it (m); رأيتها = I saw them (things); راجعت = I revised; ركبت = I rode, I took (a vehicle); سافرت = I travelled; سبحت = I swam; سجلته = I recorded it; سمعت = I heard; سمعته = I heard it; سمعتها = I heard it (f)
errors.problem: an unvocalised past verb ending in ـت covers -tu (I), -ta (you m), -ti (you f) and -at (she/it); each gloss fixes one person taken from one sentence, so حَجَزْتُ 'I booked' is shown as '(she) booked', رَأَيْتُ 'I saw' as 'you saw', اشْتَرَيْتَ 'you bought' as 'I bought'. رأيتها 'I saw them (things)' and اتفقت '(-i links to the next word)' also leak sentence-specific notes
errors.fix: give the person set, e.g. حجزت = I booked (ḥajaztu); you booked (-ta/-ti); she booked (ḥajazat) · رأيت = I saw; you saw (to a man / to a woman) · رأيتها = I saw it (f), her, them (things); you saw … · أحضرت = I brought; you brought; she brought · اتفقت = I agreed; you agreed; she agreed — same pattern for every key in this list (the object suffix -هُ / -هَا stays as glossed)

errors.path: أرسله; أحضرها; أصبح; أخبرنا; أحضرنا; ساعدنا
errors.current: أرسله = (he) sent it (m); أحضرها = (he) brought it; أصبح = (he) became, has become; أخبرنا = (he) told us; أحضرنا = we brought; ساعدنا = (he) helped us
errors.problem: Form IV past 'he …' and Form IV present 'I …' share the spelling: أُرْسِلُهُ 'I send it', أُحْضِرُهَا 'I bring it', أُصْبِحُ 'I become'. And ـنا covers both 'we …' (أَخْبَرْنَا we told, سَاعَدْنَا we helped) and '… us' (أَحْضَرَنَا he brought us). Each gloss gives one side only
errors.fix: أرسله = (he) sent it (m); I send it · أحضرها = (he) brought it (f); I bring it · أصبح = (he) became; I become · أخبرنا = (he) told us (akhbaranā); we told (akhbarnā) · أحضرنا = we brought (aḥḍarnā); (he) brought us (aḥḍaranā) · ساعدنا = (he) helped us (sāʿadanā); we helped (sāʿadnā)

errors.current: زارنا = (they) visited us
errors.problem: زَارَنَا is singular 'he visited us'; '(they)' is the plural subject that follows the verb in one sentence (زرنا 'we visited' and زاروا 'they visited' are separate keys)
errors.fix: (he) visited us (singular form, also used before a plural subject)

errors.current: أنظف = cleaner; أحدث = newer, more modern
errors.problem: key also covers the Form II present: أُنَظِّف 'I clean' and أُحَدِّث 'I talk to, I tell' (اَلتَّنْظِيف / حدثني are both course words), so the elative-only gloss is wrong for those taps
errors.fix: أنظف = cleaner (anẓaf); I clean (unaẓẓif) · أحدث = newer, more modern (aḥdath); I talk to, I tell (uḥaddith)

errors.path: ابنك; اتصالك; ساعتك; خطتك; أريك; إنك; بأنك
errors.current: ابنك = your son (to a woman); اتصالك = your call (to a woman); ساعتك = your watch (to a woman); خطتك = your plan (to a woman); أريك = I show you (to a woman); إنك = that you (to a woman, after qāla); بأنك = that you (to a woman)
errors.problem: unvocalised ـك covers -ka (to a man) and -ki (to a woman); these seven glosses fix the female addressee of one sentence, so a learner tapping ابْنُكَ in a line to a man is told 'to a woman' (the rest of the list uses 'to a man' as the default, which is at least the dictionary convention). إنك also leaks 'after qāla'
errors.fix: ابنك = your son (-ka to a man, -ki to a woman) · اتصالك = your call · ساعتك = your watch · خطتك = your plan · أريك = I show you · إنك = that you (inna + -ka/-ki) · بأنك = that you (bi-anna + -ka/-ki)

errors.current: ستأتي = she will come; ستقابل = she will meet; تبيع = she sells; تساعد = (she) helps ('helps'); تدخل = (they, f) enter ('can come in'); تخلع = (they) are taken off; تقل = (she) say; تنتظرك = (she) wait for you (to a man); تجعلني = makes me; تخمن = do you guess; تبدو = you look, you seem (to a man); تدرس = you study (to a man); ستحب = you will love (to a man); سترى = you will see (to a man) (and the rest of the keys in path, each glossed for one person only)
errors.problem: the prefix تـ with no suffix is both 'you (m)' and 'she/it (f)' (and تـ…ان both 'you two' and 'they two (f)'); each gloss picks the person of one sentence. Secondary leaks in the same group: تقل '(she) say' and تنتظرك '(she) wait' are ungrammatical, تدخل/تخلع give the non-human plural subject of one line, تخمن 'do you guess' and تجعلني 'makes me' are sentence fragments
errors.fix: give both persons, e.g. ستأتي = she will come; you will come (to a man) · تبيع = she sells; you sell (to a man) · تدرس = you study (to a man); she studies · تقل = she says / you say (jussive, after lam or lā) · تنتظرك = she waits for you; (to a man) · تجعلني = (she, it) makes me; you make me · تخمن = you guess (to a man); she guesses · تدخل = she / it enters; you enter (to a man) · تخلع = (it, f) is taken off; you take off · تصيران = you two become; they two (f) become — same pattern for every key in this list

For keys with a final ـي/ـو/ـا the dropped ن does mark the subjunctive/jussive, but for the others (أجلس, أحتفل, أدخل, أطبخ, تترك, تنام, تمشي …) the unvocalised key is identical to the indicative أَجْلِسُ 'I sit', so the note is misleading on most taps. أكتبها 'I write them' and تجدها/تضعها 'it (f)' also fix one referent

summary: Checked all ~1,700 entries of glossary-auto-1 (آتي … سيارتي) as dictionary glosses for an unvocalised key that must hold for every vocalisation. 28 findings: 20 major, 8 minor (many grouped, so several hundred keys are affected). Three patterns dominate. (1) Homograph keys glossed with one reading only, where the omitted reading is basic or is itself taught in the course: المدرسة (school/teacher f), الرجل/رجل/رجلان (man/leg), العام (year), العالم (scholar), الدين (religion), حرب (war), جد (grandfather), جمع (plural), جملا (sentences), درسنا (we studied), المهمة (task), أقدم (I present), أحمل/حملت (carry). (2) Sentence-specific person leaked into verb glosses: every past ـت form is fixed to one of I/you/she; the تـ prefix is fixed to either 'you (m)' or 'she'; Form IV he-past vs I-present (أرسله) and ـنا 'we' vs 'us' (أخبرنا) are one-sided; Form II/IV/VIII/X past and imperative (اتصل, استعمل) are given as one or the other. (3) The most dangerous group: jussive forms after لا glossed as bare positive imperatives (تخف 'be afraid', تنس 'forget', تقلقي 'worry'), which teach the opposite of لا تَخَفْ 'don't be afraid', plus تأخذها given as an imperative; and the leaked contradiction خالتك ('your cousin'). Minor findings cover leaked case/mood notes ('after kāna', 'after an', '(object)'), gendered -k glosses fixed to 'to a woman', and quoted sentence translations ('I was afraid', 'good night'). Nouns, numbers, names, place names, months, colours and the ال‑ nouns are otherwise accurate; the second-sense omissions listed in notes are low risk.
